items.text: 7 If you add some powdered aluminium to a small amount of cold dilute hydrochloric acid in a boiling tube, very little happens. If you warm this gently, it starts to fizz very rapidly.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a State the name of the gas given off to produce the fizzing.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b If you used an excess of hydrochloric acid, the result would be a colourless solution. State the name of the solution.

items.label: list_item
items.text: cWrite the full balanced equation for the reaction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: d Explain why the aluminium hardly reacts at all with the dilute acid in the cold, but reacts vigorously after even gentle heating.

items.label: list_item
items.text: 8 If you have some small pieces of the metal titanium and any simple apparatus that you might need, describe how you would find out the approximate position of titanium in the reactivity series, using only water and dilute hydrochloric acid. You only need to find out that the reactivity is 'similar to iron' or 'similar to magnesium', for example. Your experiments should be done in an order that guarantees maximum safety. For example, if titanium's reactivity turned out to be similar to potassium, dropping it into dilute hydrochloric acid wouldn't be a good idea!

items.text: 9 In the past, cars were made from mild steel, which was then painted. In more modern cars, the mild steel is galvanised before it is painted.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a State the conditions under which iron/steel rusts.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Explain how painting prevents iron/steel from rusting.

items.label: list_item
items.text: c What is meant by galvanised steel?

items.label: list_item
items.text: d Describe and explain the effect that galvanised steel has on the life of the car.
